solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unlimited entry as a caller's case is re-examined

indicators.note: re-examining a case turns its contents over afresh, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gets admitted everywhere because a phone caller's legal case is being looked at again.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass with this name lets the holder into every part of a venue, so entry has no limits.

clue.text: Shooter!

parts.note: a shooter looks like a gunman, but a person who shoots film is meant

explanation.surface: An alarmed cry that someone has a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Film crews speak of shooting a scene, so the person operating the camera is the one who shoots.

clue.text: The poet's inspiration drawn from godlier atonement

indicators.note: letters drawn from a phrase are pulled out of the run of words godlier atonement

explanation.surface: A poet takes inspiration from religious penitence.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, a source of inspiration for poets.

clue.text: Mrs Cooke given a right big kiss!

indicators.note: set right means put in order, here rearranging the letters of the name and the a

explanation.surface: A woman called Mrs Cooke receives a real smacker of a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' reads as the intensifier in 'a right big kiss' but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Smackeroo is informal slang for a loud, hearty kiss, a smacker.

clue.text: Name capitals of Laos, Latvia, Oman, Yemen and Djibouti

indicators.note: capitals here are capital letters, the first letter of each country named

explanation.surface: A quiz instruction to give the capital cities of five countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' wants capital cities; it means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lloyd is a forename and surname, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: It slides down over husband inside a bed cover

indicators.note: inside means the husband's letter is placed within the following words

parts.note: a valance is a decorative drape around the base of a bed

explanation.surface: Something slides down over a husband who is tucked in under a bed cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow and ice that rushes down a mountainside is exactly something that slides down.

clue.text: Record Scottish impatience this time

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
och is a Scots exclamation of impatience or regret

explanation.surface: A Scot tuts impatiently at a record this time round.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a distinct period or era, a span of time.

clue.text: Support environmental conservation when ability's there

indicators.note: the clue says the answer becomes the longer phrase when the second word is added, so the answer is that phrase minus it
'there' marks that the word ability is present in the longer phrase and must be taken away to leave the answer

parts.note: sustainability is the green ideal of conserving the environment
ability is taken as written

explanation.surface: A green slogan about backing conservation when one has the means.
explanation.walkthrough: Add ABILITY to the answer and you get SUSTAINABILITY, environmental conservation; so the answer is that word with ABILITY removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to bear its weight or keep it going, to support it.

clue.text: Cloth to wrap around end of gardener's tool

indicators.note: wrapping around means the cloth's letters surround the next piece

parts.note: a towel is a cloth for drying
the last letter of gardener is R

explanation.surface: A cloth is wrapped round the end of a gardener's implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool with a blade, used in gardening and plastering.

clue.text: Architects' hesitation, standing in for one dance

indicators.note: standing in for means one piece replaces another, here the hesitation replaces the one

parts.note: RIBA is the Royal Institute of British Architects
I is the Roman numeral one
um is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: Architects hesitate, one of them deputising for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: RIBA is the Royal Institute of British Architects, the UK professional body.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Irregular sections of another male louse

indicators.note: only sections of the words another, male and louse are kept, the rest of each word being cut away

explanation.surface: A biologist notes odd segments on yet another male louse.
explanation.walkthrough: The chunks are uneven: ANO from 'another', MA from 'male', LOUS from 'louse', dropping THER, LE and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anomalous departs from the norm, so it is out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Magician's struggle to get embrace

definitions.note: read as 'magician is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: war is a struggle or conflict
a lock is a tight hold, as in a wrestling embrace

explanation.surface: A conjurer has to fight to get a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: A warlock is a male witch or sorcerer, one who works magic.

clue.text: Back in the morning (early hour) to get plastic money?

indicators.note: back means the whole assembly is read from end to start

parts.note: AM is ante meridiem, in the morning

indicators.note: early means the first letter of hour

parts.note: a card is plastic money, a credit or debit card

explanation.surface: Getting up early to fetch a credit card in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: AM, H and CARD give AMHCARD, which read backwards makes the answer; the question mark flags that plastic is not this old currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the currency of Greece before the euro, a unit of money.

clue.text: Dance up in the air

definitions.meaning: a dance where one bends backwards under a low bar
undecided, in a state of uncertainty

explanation.surface: A dance performed airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar-dance shares its name with the state of waiting in uncertainty, being unresolved.

clue.text: Done with the rest? On the contrary!

definitions.text: Done with the rest? On the contrary!

parts.words: Done with the rest? On the contrary!
parts.note: finished with rest suggests waking up; the opposite is rest going past the time you meant to rise: rest that is done to excess

explanation.surface: Asking if someone has finished resting, then insisting the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the order of 'done' (over) and 'rest' (sleep) and you have the answer, rest carried on too long.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to wake at the intended time is to keep slumbering past it.

clue.text: Communist effort directed at literary improvement

parts.note: red is a standard nickname for a Communist
action is effort or activity

explanation.surface: A Communist campaign aimed at improving literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Redaction is the editing of a text for publication, a way of improving writing.

clue.text: It protects Tess and Henry, playing in musical union

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the musical piece

parts.note: a duet unites two performers in music

indicators.note: playing about with letters moves them into a new order

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Tess and Henry perform together in a musical duet that guards them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the name and H, and 'in' sets the result inside the duet; H is the symbol for the henry, a physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth laid over furniture to keep dust off it serves to protect.

clue.text: Aren't Ali and I unruly (among other things)?

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether Ali and the speaker are badly behaved, among other faults.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is the Latin phrase for among other things, used in formal writing.

clue.text: Heavy matter holding Oscar's faulty drone

indicators.note: holding means the matter surrounds the following pieces

parts.note: pus is the matter in an infected wound
Oscar is O in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: faulty means the letters of drone are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A weighty substance encloses a broken-down drone belonging to Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' scrambles the drone, and 'holding' wraps the matter round Oscar's letter plus that scramble; 'matter' here is the discharge from a wound, not physical substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponderous means weighty and slow-moving, so it describes something heavy.

clue.text: US city cop arrests working relative (Spanish aunt)

indicators.note: a cop who arrests someone holds them, so the officer's letters go round the rest

parts.note: PC is a police constable
on means working or operating
tia is Spanish for aunt

explanation.surface: A US police officer arrests a working relative, a Spanish aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontiac is a city in Michigan, also the name of a former car brand.

clue.text: Enid is to put it away

parts.note: read the answer's two words as wordplay: eat gives DINE, and up writes it upwards, which gives the clue's name

explanation.surface: A woman named Enid is told to tidy something away.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, builds the clue word. 'Put it away' is slang for eating heartily.
explanation.definitionFit: To put food away is informal for consuming it, finishing it all off.

clue.text: Boy overcome by sharp sound over fence

indicators.note: being overcome by something means being held inside it, so the boy goes within the sound

parts.note: a ping is a short high ringing sound
Al is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad is startled by a sharp crack from beyond a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A paling is a fence made of pointed stakes, or one such stake.

clue.text: They are ready to reveal the bare facts

definitions.text: They are ready to reveal the bare facts

parts.words: They are ready to reveal the bare facts
parts.note: seems to describe frank reporters, but describes people happy to bare all, the bare facts being their bodies

explanation.surface: Some people are willing to tell the plain truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists who go without clothes are ready to show their bare bodies.

clue.text: Girl opens paper inmate needs to draw on

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name

indicators.note: the openings of words are their first letters, taken from the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A girl opens the newspaper an inmate needs to draw on.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip into savings or resources is to draw on them.

clue.text: Flight into imperialist airspace

indicators.note: into here means the answer lies within the words imperialist airspace

explanation.surface: A plane flies into an imperial power's airspace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests an aircraft, but it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a series of steps, and one step of it carries the same name.

clue.text: Number of times Les goes back to woman indoors

indicators.note: indoors means the woman is placed inside the reversed name
going back means Les is read from end to start

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Les keeps returning to a woman who stays at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes back' reverses the name and 'indoors' houses the woman within it; 'times' is surface padding the blogger also found hard to place.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means more than two but not many, an indefinite number.

clue.text: A snake and a sneak?

definitions.meaning: a treacherous person, someone spiteful who betrays others

explanation.surface: Asking whether a snake is also a sneak.
explanation.definitionFit: The venomous reptile also names a malicious, treacherous person, a snake in the grass.

clue.text: Swear one member's on about returning Greek character

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
re means on, concerning
c, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: returning means the Greek letter is read backwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A politician goes on about a Greek character and is told off for swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: C is circa, Latin for about. 'returning' turns ETA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprecate is to utter curses, so it means to swear.

clue.text: Tower of power

parts.note: sounds like a description of someone mighty, but is a tall structure carrying power lines

explanation.surface: A phrase for a commanding figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall steel structure holding electricity cables is a tower that carries power.

clue.text: Undercover sting against criminal Paris tailor

parts.note: a con is a swindle, a sting

indicators.note: criminal means wrong, so the letters are bent out of their order

explanation.surface: An undercover sting operation against a crooked Parisian tailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspiratorial describes secret plotting, behaviour carried out covertly.
